name: Ethical and Professional Standards
description: The CFA Institute Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct and the Asset Manager Code: duties to clients, employers and markets, including loyalty, fair dealing, suitability, conflicts and material non-public information.
l1: Knows the Code and the seven Standards (professionalism, market integrity, duties to clients and to employers, investment analysis, conflicts, CFA responsibilities) and what the Asset Manager Code adds for firms.
l2: Applies the Standards in their own work: discloses conflicts, allocates trades fairly, checks suitability, keeps records that support recommendations, and protects confidential and material non-public information.
l3: Resolves ambiguous cases for a team (personal trading, soft dollars, pressure on research), writes compliance procedures such as a code of ethics or trade-allocation policy, and trains colleagues.
l4: Sits on a body that writes or enforces investment ethics (CFA Institute Standards of Practice Council or Disciplinary Review Committee, a regulator's panel) or writes guidance the profession uses.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Quantitative Methods
description: Quantitative tools for investment work: time value of money, probability distributions, sampling and estimation, regression, time-series forecasting, volatility models, simulation, model validation, machine learning and generative AI.
l1: Knows time value of money, distributions, hypothesis tests, regression and time-series models, simulation, and where machine learning and large language models fit, with their assumptions and failure modes.
l2: Builds and interprets regression, time-series or simulation models on investment data, checks assumptions such as heteroskedasticity, serial correlation and stationarity, and backtests the results.
l3: Designs and validates models for a team (backtests, out-of-sample tests, monitoring), spots overfitted or spurious results, and reviews others' models before they drive decisions.
l4: Develops quantitative methods others adopt, publishes in journals such as the Financial Analysts Journal, or sets model governance standards for an institution.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Economics
description: Micro- and macroeconomics as they affect markets: firms and industry structure, business cycles, inflation, monetary and fiscal policy, trade and currencies, growth, regulation, geopolitics and capital market expectations.
l1: Knows how supply and demand, cycles, inflation, policy, trade flows and exchange-rate models work, and how economic indicators feed capital market expectations.
l2: Uses growth, inflation, policy and currency analysis to support forecasts and asset views in their own recommendations.
l3: Builds the economic outlook and capital market expectations behind a team's allocation decisions, tests them with scenarios, and defends them to an investment committee.
l4: Publishes economic outlooks or research cited beyond their firm, or advises central banks, governments or large institutions on policy or market expectations.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Financial Statement Analysis
description: Analysing financial statements under IFRS and US GAAP: reporting quality, off-balance-sheet items, employee compensation, intercorporate investments, foreign operations, banks and insurers, and building a company financial model.
l1: Knows how the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement link, the main ratios, and where IFRS and US GAAP choices change reported results.
l2: Analyses a company's statements, adjusts for accounting choices (leases, pensions, intercorporate investments, currency translation), judges earnings quality and builds a three-statement model.
l3: Leads complex or forensic analysis for a team (aggressive revenue recognition, off-balance-sheet risk, bank and insurer statements), signs off others' models and coaches analysts.
l4: Contributes to accounting standard setting (IASB, FASB or AcSB advisory groups and comment letters), gives expert evidence on financial reporting, or publishes analysis methods peers rely on.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Corporate Finance
description: How companies are structured, owned, governed and financed: stakeholder and governance issues, ESG risk factors, capital investment, capital structure and cost of capital, payouts, and mergers, acquisitions and restructuring.
l1: Knows governance mechanisms, capital budgeting (NPV, IRR), the cost of capital and capital structure choices, and how mergers, spin-offs and restructurings affect value.
l2: Evaluates capital projects with NPV and IRR, estimates a weighted average cost of capital, and assesses a company's leverage, payout and governance.
l3: Advises on capital structure, investment or restructuring decisions for complex companies, accountable for the recommendation, and reviews others' analyses.
l4: Advises boards of other organisations on major transactions (fairness opinions, recapitalisations, M&A), or shapes governance codes and practice beyond their own firm.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Equities
description: Equity investment: security types and markets, industry and company analysis, valuing individual stocks (dividend, free cash flow, residual income and multiples models), equity market valuation, shorting and ESG factors.
l1: Knows equity markets and indexes, industry and competitive analysis, and the main valuation models: dividend discount, free cash flow, residual income and price multiples.
l2: Analyses industries and companies and values equities with discounted cash flow, residual income and multiples, producing a research note with a target price.
l3: Leads coverage of a sector, makes and defends buy or sell recommendations to an investment committee, and reviews and mentors other analysts' work.
l4: An analyst or investor whose published research, rankings or valuation methods others follow, or who teaches equity valuation on professional programmes.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Fixed Income
description: Fixed income: security types and markets, term structure and spreads, bond valuation, interest-rate risk (duration and convexity), credit risk, bonds with embedded options, and securitised products.
l1: Knows bond features, yield and spread measures, the term structure, duration and convexity, credit ratings, and how embedded options and securitisation change risk.
l2: Prices bonds, measures duration and convexity, values bonds with embedded options on a binomial tree, and analyses an issuer's credit risk.
l3: Leads analysis of complex instruments (callable, convertible, mortgage-backed and other securitised products), sets credit views for a team and reviews others' work.
l4: Shapes credit or rates views beyond their firm (rating committee chair, widely cited research) or develops fixed income valuation methods others use.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Derivatives and Risk Management
description: Forwards, futures, options and swaps: no-arbitrage pricing (binomial and Black-Scholes-Merton models), their use in portfolios, currency hedging and management, and risk management.
l1: Knows how forwards, futures, options and swaps work, the no-arbitrage basis of their pricing, and how they hedge equity, rate and currency exposure.
l2: Prices and uses derivatives to hedge or adjust portfolio exposures (duration, beta, currency), and measures the hedge's cost and effectiveness.
l3: Designs hedging and risk programmes (overlays, value-at-risk and stress-test limits) for a portfolio or institution, and oversees others' use of derivatives.
l4: Sets risk frameworks adopted by institutions, advises regulators or industry bodies on derivatives and risk, or develops pricing or risk methods others adopt.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Alternative Investments
description: Alternative investments: real estate, real assets (infrastructure, timber, farmland), private equity, private credit and venture capital, hedge funds, commodities and digital assets, with their structures, fees and risks.
l1: Knows the main alternative asset classes, their vehicles, fee and return structures, valuation approaches, and risks such as illiquidity and smoothed reported returns.
l2: Analyses and values an alternative investment (a property by direct capitalisation or DCF, or a fund's fees and returns) and assesses its role in a portfolio.
l3: Selects and monitors alternative managers and investments for an institutional portfolio, runs their due diligence and advises an investment committee.
l4: Shapes due diligence or allocation practice for alternatives beyond their own organisation, for example through ILPA or industry guidelines, published research or advice to large funds.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Portfolio Construction
description: Building and revising portfolios: the investment policy statement, portfolio theory, vehicles such as ETFs, indexing, behavioural finance, taxes, individual and institutional portfolios, and managing equity, fixed income and alternatives portfolios.
l1: Knows the investment policy statement, mean-variance and factor models, diversification, vehicles, behavioural biases, and how taxes and constraints shape individual and institutional portfolios.
l2: Writes an investment policy statement, then builds and rebalances a portfolio to it within its risk, return, liquidity and tax constraints.
l3: Designs portfolio construction and rebalancing processes for multi-asset mandates and reviews other managers' portfolios against their policies.
l4: Develops construction methods adopted across an organisation or the industry, or publishes portfolio research that others cite.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Asset Allocation
description: Asset allocation: setting capital market expectations, strategic and tactical allocation, allocation methods such as mean-variance and liability-relative, and goals-based allocation.
l1: Knows how capital market expectations are formed and how strategic, tactical, liability-relative and goals-based allocations are set and rebalanced.
l2: Prepares capital market expectations and a strategic allocation proposal, with rebalancing ranges, for a portfolio.
l3: Leads asset allocation for institutional or multi-client portfolios, sets tactical tilts and defends the policy to investment committees.
l4: Advises large pension, endowment or sovereign funds on policy portfolios, or publishes allocation research others in the industry adopt.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Performance Measurement
description: Measuring and evaluating performance: return calculation, attribution and appraisal, benchmarks, GIPS-compliant presentation, investment manager selection, and evaluating trade execution.
l1: Knows time- and money-weighted returns, attribution, risk-adjusted measures (Sharpe ratio, information ratio), benchmark properties, GIPS requirements and manager selection criteria.
l2: Calculates returns, runs attribution against a benchmark and reports performance, or prepares a GIPS composite presentation or a manager evaluation.
l3: Oversees performance measurement and GIPS compliance for a firm, and evaluates and recommends managers to a committee.
l4: Verifies other firms' GIPS compliance as an independent verifier, or contributes to the GIPS standards or industry performance standards through CFA Institute committees.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Index Investing
description: Index investing: index construction and weighting, market efficiency, passive strategies, tracking error, and index funds and ETFs.
l1: Knows how indexes are constructed, weighted and rebalanced, the case for passive management, and the sources of tracking error.
l2: Implements an index-tracking portfolio by full replication, sampling or optimisation, and manages its tracking error, rebalancing and costs.
l3: Designs index strategies or custom benchmarks and advises on passive, factor and active choices for a mandate.
l4: Sits on an index provider's methodology committee, or designs indexes or ETF strategies that are widely used.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Fixed Income Portfolio Management
description: Managing fixed income portfolios: liability-based mandates (immunisation, cash-flow matching), total-return mandates, and yield-curve, credit and currency strategies.
l1: Knows liability-based and total-return mandates and the main yield-curve, credit and currency strategies.
l2: Implements duration, curve and credit positioning in a portfolio and measures its exposures against a benchmark.
l3: Manages fixed income portfolios through rate and credit cycles, accountable for results, and leads the strategy for a team.
l4: A fixed income manager whose strategy or published research other managers study or follow.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Equity Portfolio Management
description: Managing equity portfolios: passive and active approaches, styles and factor exposures, active risk budgeting, and the equity manager's investment process.
l1: Knows passive, factor and active equity approaches, style analysis, and how active risk is budgeted.
l2: Implements an equity strategy and monitors its factor and style exposures, active share and tracking error.
l3: Manages equity portfolios to a defined process, explains performance through attribution, and guides other managers.
l4: An equity manager whose process or research other managers use as a reference.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Execution of Portfolio Decisions (including Trading and Market Microstructure)
description: Executing portfolio decisions: order types, trading venues and market microstructure, trading costs, algorithmic trading, best execution and trade evaluation.
l1: Knows order types, venues, bid-ask spreads and market impact, and how implementation shortfall and VWAP measure trading cost.
l2: Chooses a trading strategy for each order, evaluates execution against benchmarks such as implementation shortfall, and documents best execution.
l3: Designs trading and best-execution policy for a portfolio team, reviews execution quality and challenges brokers on cost.
l4: Shapes trading practice or market structure beyond their firm, for example through regulator consultations or industry trading committees.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Management of Institutional Investor Portfolios
description: Managing institutional portfolios: defined benefit pensions, endowments and foundations, insurers, banks and sovereign wealth funds, with their objectives, constraints, governance and investment policies.
l1: Knows the return objectives, liabilities, liquidity needs and governance of the main institutional investors.
l2: Prepares an investment policy and portfolio recommendation for an institutional client.
l3: Advises institutional boards and investment committees on policy, allocation and governance, accountable for the advice.
l4: Advises major funds outside their own organisation, or shapes institutional governance practice through pension or endowment industry guidance.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Liability - Driven Investments (including Asset Liability Management and Goal-Based investing)
description: Liability-driven and goals-based investing: immunisation and cash-flow matching, asset-liability management for pensions and insurers, and goals-based portfolios for individuals.
l1: Knows immunisation, cash-flow and duration matching, surplus management, and how goals-based investing splits wealth into goal portfolios.
l2: Builds a liability-hedging or goals-based portfolio and measures how well it matches its liabilities or goals (hedge ratio, funded status).
l3: Designs asset-liability programmes for pensions, insurers or families and advises on their interest-rate, longevity and funding risks.
l4: Advises large plans or insurers outside their own organisation on asset-liability management, or publishes LDI methods the industry adopts.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Long/Short Portfolio Management
description: Long/short portfolio management: shorting mechanics and costs, securities lending, leverage, market-neutral and other long/short strategies, and their risks.
l1: Knows how shorting, securities lending, margin and leverage work, and the risks of long/short and market-neutral strategies.
l2: Implements long/short positions and manages their gross and net exposure, borrowing costs and margin.
l3: Runs long/short strategies with risk limits (gross, net, factor, crowding), accountable for results, and guides others in them.
l4: A long/short manager whose approach others study or follow, or who shapes industry practice on shorting and leverage.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Deal Origination, Screening, Analysis, and Valuation
description: Finding and assessing private-market deals: sourcing, screening, due diligence, analysis and valuation of private companies and assets.
l1: Knows how private deals are sourced and screened, the due diligence workstreams, and private valuation methods (DCF, comparables, LBO analysis).
l2: Screens opportunities, runs due diligence workstreams, and builds valuations and investment committee memos.
l3: Leads deals from origination to investment committee, accountable for the recommendation, and guides deal teams.
l4: Shapes private-market sourcing or valuation practice beyond their firm, for example through the IPEV Valuation Guidelines, published methods or industry training.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Deal Structuring, Financing, and Negotiation
description: Structuring, financing and negotiating private deals: capital structure, senior and mezzanine debt, equity terms, covenants and protections, and negotiation.
l1: Knows deal structures, debt and equity financing options, covenants, and key terms such as preferences, earn-outs and governance rights.
l2: Models deal structures and financing, such as an LBO model with debt tranches, and supports negotiation of terms.
l3: Leads structuring and negotiation of complex transactions, accountable for the terms agreed.
l4: Consulted beyond their firm on deal structuring and terms, or shapes market-standard deal documents.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Management of Assets, Execution of Value Creation Strategies, and Exit Strategies
description: Owning and exiting private investments: governance, value creation plans, operational improvement, monitoring, and exit routes such as trade sale, IPO and secondary sale.
l1: Knows how value creation plans, portfolio monitoring and exit routes (trade sale, IPO, secondary sale, recapitalisation) work.
l2: Monitors portfolio companies or assets and tracks value creation against plan with KPIs and board reporting.
l3: Leads value creation and exit strategies for portfolio investments, accountable for the outcome.
l4: Shapes value creation or exit practice beyond their firm, through board roles across sponsors, published case work or industry teaching.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Fund Vehicles, Agreements, and Structures
description: Private fund vehicles and agreements: limited partnerships, limited partnership agreements (LPAs), side letters, governance, investor rights and key terms.
l1: Knows the main fund structures and LPA terms: commitment period, fees, carried interest, key-person and removal clauses, and side letters.
l2: Reviews fund terms and agreements and explains their effect to investors or managers.
l3: Negotiates fund terms and structures vehicles for managers or investors, accountable for the terms.
l4: Shapes market terms beyond their firm, for example through ILPA Principles and Model LPA work or industry committees.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Capital Flows: Raising Capital, Distributing Returns, and Collecting Fees/Carried Interest
description: Capital flows in private funds: fundraising, capital calls, distributions, waterfalls, management fees and carried interest.
l1: Knows capital calls, distributions, European and American waterfalls, hurdle rates, catch-up and clawback.
l2: Models a fund's cash flows, distribution waterfall, fees and carried interest.
l3: Designs fee and waterfall structures and leads fundraising or investor relations.
l4: Consulted beyond their firm on fund economics and market practice, for example through ILPA reporting templates or industry fee studies.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Private Asset Classes: Market Context, Investment Strategies and Investment Process
description: Private asset classes (private equity, private credit, real estate, infrastructure, natural resources): their markets, strategies and investment process.
l1: Knows the main private asset classes, their strategies, return drivers and risks, and how a private-markets investment process runs.
l2: Analyses opportunities and managers within one private asset class.
l3: Sets strategy and builds programmes across private asset classes, including commitment pacing.
l4: An authority on private markets whose strategy views or research others outside their organisation follow.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Measures of Fund Level Returns and Performance at Portfolio Company Level
description: Measuring private market performance: IRR, multiples (TVPI, DPI, RVPI), public market equivalents, and benchmarking at fund and portfolio-company level.
l1: Knows IRR, TVPI, DPI and RVPI, public market equivalents, and why interim fund returns are hard to compare.
l2: Calculates and benchmarks fund and portfolio-company returns.
l3: Evaluates managers and programmes on performance and explains the results to committees.
l4: Develops or maintains private-market performance measures or benchmarks that others use.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Private Wealth Management Industry
description: The private wealth management industry: firm types, business models, services, regulation and the adviser's role.
l1: Knows how wealth firms are organised, paid and regulated (CIRO and provincial securities regulators in Canada; the SEC and FINRA in the US) and the adviser's duties.
l2: Delivers a wealth firm's services to clients within its regulatory and compliance requirements.
l3: Shapes the service model, pricing and practice of a wealth team.
l4: Shapes wealth management practice beyond their firm through industry bodies, regulators or published work.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Client Management
description: Managing private clients: discovery, communication, behavioural finance, trust and the long-term relationship.
l1: Knows the stages of the client relationship, discovery techniques and common behavioural biases.
l2: Runs discovery, documents the client's goals and risk profile, communicates recommendations and manages the relationship.
l3: Manages complex family and high-net-worth relationships and coaches other advisers.
l4: Develops client-relationship methods that other wealth firms or professional programmes adopt.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Wealth Planning
description: Wealth planning for individuals and families: tax, estate, retirement, insurance, philanthropy and succession (in Canada, for example, RRSPs, TFSAs, trusts and deemed disposition at death).
l1: Knows the main areas of wealth planning and how tax, estate, retirement and insurance decisions interact.
l2: Prepares a wealth plan covering cash flow, tax, retirement, estate and insurance needs.
l3: Coordinates complex plans with tax, legal and estate specialists for wealthy families.
l4: A wealth planning authority consulted by other advisers or professional bodies, or who teaches planning on professional programmes.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: Investment Management
description: Managing investments for private clients: portfolios fitted to goals, taxes and constraints, asset location, tax-loss harvesting, concentrated positions and ongoing review.
l1: Knows how private client portfolios differ from institutional ones: taxes, asset location, concentrated positions and changing goals.
l2: Builds and reviews tax-aware portfolios for private clients.
l3: Leads investment management for complex private client portfolios and reviews other advisers' portfolios.
l4: An authority on private client investing whose approach other firms or programmes adopt.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)

name: HNW Client Profiling & Asset Allocation
description: Profiling high-net-worth clients and allocating their assets: goals, risk tolerance and capacity, liquidity, concentrated positions and family structures.
l1: Knows risk tolerance and capacity profiling, goals-based allocation, and how concentrated or illiquid wealth changes the allocation.
l2: Profiles clients and recommends allocations that fit their goals and constraints.
l3: Handles complex profiles (concentrated wealth, family businesses, multigenerational families) and guides other advisers.
l4: An authority on HNW profiling and allocation whose methods other firms adopt.
source: Drafted for the graph from the CFA Program CBOK topic areas and sub-areas (2027 curriculum)
